hyps.why: A skip on edge 2 keeps gradients flowing so the conv on edge 5 adds capacity rather than competing for optimization.
With edge 2 already a conv, upgrading edge 5 is redundant capacity and yields diminishing returns.
A pooled, blurred input from node 2 limits what a 3x3 conv on edge 5 can extract, especially on low-resolution ImageNet16-120.
Edge 4 reads node 1, which is blurred by a pool on edge 0, so a larger conv kernel gains little.
Replacing none adds a whole new path to node 2, which gains more than upgrading an existing op.
Replacing an existing pool is a smaller upgrade than filling an empty edge, so the gain is smaller.
The direct 0->3 shortcut already supplies a clean path to the output, so extra conv capacity on edge 4 is partly redundant.
The edge 3 shortcut bypasses the conv path and reduces the marginal benefit of upgrading edge 5.
A strong early conv on the non-adjacent edge 0 produces richer features that a final-stage conv on edge 5 can exploit.
Without the direct 0->3 shortcut, the conv paths through node 2 carry more of the output, so upgrading edge 1 matters more.
